claims.reason: Passage 4 states Jack Lindsey leads Anthropic's 'model psychiatry' team and concludes models show at least a limited, functional form of introspective awareness that is highly limited and context-dependent.

Passage 5 confirms Chris Olah and Josh Batson work on circuit-tracing research that found the 'can't answer' default pathway and their publications are the main source for mechanistic explanations of hallucination.
Passage 6 directly states Sam Marks has worked on how models represent truth internally (the 'geometry of truth' line) and on auditing models for hidden objectives.
Passage 8 identifies Sebastian Farquhar and Yarin Gal as lead authors of the 2024 Nature semantic entropy paper, the best-known method for detecting confabulations by sampling multiple answers.

Passage 9 describes Adam Tauman Kalai's 2025 paper 'Why Language Models Hallucinate' arguing that training and evaluation reward guessing over admitting uncertainty, essential for understanding the incentive problem.
Passage 10 notes Owain Evans has done influential work on whether models know what they know, including teaching models to express uncertainty in words and describing their learned behaviors.
Passage 12 states Stephen Fleming is a leading neuroscientist of human metacognition who applies metacognition research to AI, clarifying the calibration-versus-discrimination distinction.
Passage 14 says Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor wrote an agent reliability paper borrowing from nuclear and aviation safety and produce a skeptical, data-driven newsletter.
Passage 15 states METR measures how long agents can complete tasks autonomously and their reports are a key reference for reliability-over-horizon.
Passage 16 says Andrej Karpathy popularized the 'march of nines' framing and writes clearly about moving from demos to products.
Passage 17 states Azalia Mirhoseini co-led the LLM-as-a-Verifier work on scaling verification as its own axis.

Passage 19 describes Shreya Shankar's research on LLM pipeline evaluation, including the paper 'Who Validates the Validators?' aligning automated judges with human judgment to address verifier reliability.
Passage 20 identifies Hamel Husain as a practical voice on building evals for real products, emphasizing error analysis, reading traces, and designing checks that catch real failures.
Passage 21 states Eugene Yan writes accessible, practical pieces on LLM evaluation and production patterns.

Passage 23 outlines a minimal follow set: Anthropic interpretability publications, Princeton newsletter, METR, Husain and Shankar for engineering practice, plus arXiv searches for metacognition, calibration, selective prediction, and process verifier.
Passages 1 and 2 show Kirill R advising that affiliations change often, so it's worth checking researchers' latest pages.
